You can follow progress here:
http://packages.renjin.org/qa/dashboard

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: doubleMatrixBuilder length error
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
Thanks very much for the commit. The error is cleared, but I'm now seeing an error about the dim(X) attribute because when I use if my matrix is m.inputMatrix and i use m.inputMatrix.build(), the matrix is actually being put into R as a double and not a Matrix as it was before. Is there something else I would have to add when using DoubleMatrixBuilder?
here is the part that creates the matrix:

int columnCount = listModel.size();

List<CyRow> rows = table.getAllRows();

NameMatrix m = new NameMatrix();

m.data = new double[rowCount][];

m.inputMatrix = new DoubleMatrixBuilder(m.rowCount,m.columnCount);

//m.doubleVector = new DoubleVector();

for (int i = 0; i <rowCount; i++) {

m.data[i] = new double[columnCount];

for (int j = 0; j < columnCount; j++){

m.data[i][j] = rows.get(i).get(selectedColumns.get(j).getName(), Double.class);

m.inputMatrix.set(i,j,m.data[i][j]);

}

}

return m;

}

And then the matrix is put into R as :

engine.put("x", m.inputMatrix.build());

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: doubleMatrixBuilder length error
messages.body_plain:
R is funny that way... a matrix in R is actually just a double (DoubleVector) or integer (IntVector) with a special "dim" attribute. The DoubleMatrixBuilder sets this attribute in the constructor (AbstractMatrixBuilder:22 <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/306865e16871874e3e50b8c1455868c7014659ab/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/primitives/matrix/AbstractMatrixBuilder.java#L22-L22>), so the result of m.inputMatrix.build() *should* have a "dim" attribute that is an integer vector with (numRows, numCols).

If you step through the code you might be able to see if this is indeed the case or if the dim attribute is getting dropped afterward...

Best,
Alex
